name: unity-ecosystem
description: Multi-arm evaluation manifest for Unity CLI and MCP servers (Official, Community, Specialized & CLIs)

arms.name: Official Unity CLI (com.unity.pipeline)
arms.install_hint: Ships with the com.unity.pipeline package in the Unity project; `unity upgrade --check` reports the installed version.

arms.name: Official Unity MCP (com.unity.ai.assistant)
arms.install_hint: Same `unity` CLI as official-unity-cli; register it with your harness at LOCAL scope pinned to this project, or it binds elsewhere.

arms.name: CoplayDev Unity MCP
arms.install_hint: Run the provisioned tools/three-way-setup.sh to start the server, then register the Editor via Window/MCP for Unity -> Connect.

arms.name: IvanMurzak AI Game Developer (Unity-MCP)
arms.probe_reason: Its port is derived from a SHA256 of the project path into 20000-29999, so no fixed endpoint can be checked.
arms.install_hint: openupm add com.ivanmurzak.unity.mcp (the Unity plugin provisions the server itself)

install.note: The Unity plugin downloads and manages the server binary itself, so there is no separate server install. The port is derived per project (20000-29999) and can be pinned with MCP_PLUGIN_PORT. The documented client key is 'ai-game-developer'.

steps.text: Add the plugin via OpenUPM.
Or add it directly as a git dependency instead of using OpenUPM.
Open the project. The plugin downloads and manages the server binary itself; note the port it reports, since it is derived per project (20000-29999).

arms.name: AnkleBreaker Unity MCP
arms.install_hint: npx anklebreaker-unity-mcp@latest, plus the unity-mcp-plugin UPM package

steps.text: Install the Node MCP server.
Add the Unity plugin dependency (it hosts the bridge on 7890).
Reopen the Unity project so the plugin loads and binds 7890.
Register the server with your harness using client_config below.

install.note: Two separate pieces: install only one and you get a server connected to nothing. The health check probes the Unity-side bridge (127.0.0.1:7890/api/ping), which is what actually answers whether this is wired up. Licensed under a custom 'AnkleBreaker Open License v1.0', not a standard OSI licence.

arms.probe_reason: The bridge exposes a plain liveness ping, not an MCP endpoint.

steps.text: Add the UPM package (needs Unity 6000.0+, Newtonsoft JSON, Unity Recorder).

Unity: realvirtual toolbar > 'Download Python Server'. This clones the Python server into Assets/StreamingAssets/realvirtual-MCP/ with an embedded Python 3.12, and writes the client config for you. There is no scriptable equivalent.

install.note: The Python server is NOT pip- or uvx-installable; the in-Editor 'Download Python Server' button is the only documented route. The Editor hosts a websocket-sharp server on /mcp, bound to 127.0.0.1 only. The port walks 18711-18721 when busy (a second Editor takes the next one), so the port is discovered from ~/.unity-mcp/unity-mcp-status-*.json rather than assumed -- that file also names the project each instance serves. Never probe /mcp itself: it registers a real session and increments the Connected Clients count in the Editor UI.

steps.text: Install the CLI. On Windows this script fails — use the unity-cli-win-x64 release asset or cargo instead.
Add the Unity bridge package.
Verify against a running Editor.

install.note: Installs an executable named 'unity-cli' - the same name akiojin-cli, youngwoo-cli and rage-cli all use. Only one of them can own that name on PATH. On Windows the install script fails outright: detect_rid() handles only Darwin and Linux and dies on Git Bash, despite a unity-cli-win-x64 release asset existing. Use that asset directly, or `cargo install --path .` from a clone. Connects to the Editor over TCP on port 6400.

steps.text: Install the CLI (cross-platform route).
Add the Unity Connector package; it starts when Unity opens.

install.note: Installs an executable named 'unity-cli' - the same name akiojin-cli, youngwoo-cli and rage-cli all use. Only one of them can own that name on PATH. The CLI checks its version against the Connector's and refuses on mismatch; bypass with --ignore-version-mismatch. The install URLs point at the 'master' branch while the repo default is 'main' - both resolve today.

arms.name: hatayama Unity CLI Loop (uLoop)
arms.install_hint: npm install -g uloop-cli  (the binary is 'uloop', not 'unity-cli-loop')

steps.text: Install the CLI (requires Node >= 22).
Add the Unity package (OpenUPM scope io.github.hatayama.uloopmcp also works).
Verify the binary is on PATH.

install.note: Three different strings to keep straight: package 'uloop-cli', binary 'uloop', repo 'unity-cli-loop'. It was renamed from uLoopMCP at v1.0.0, so the OpenUPM scope and the npm homepage still carry the old name.

Installs an executable named 'unity-cli' - the same name akiojin-cli, youngwoo-cli and rage-cli all use. Only one of them can own that name on PATH. Different in kind from the other CLI arms: this is a Unity Hub/Editor/licence installer and runner for CI, not an Editor-automation bridge, so it needs no Unity package and no running Editor. package.json requires Node >= 24 (the README's 'v22.12+' is stale).

steps.text: Install the CLI (requires Node >= 24).

arms.name: CoderGamester MCP Unity
arms.probe_reason: The Editor hosts a websocket-sharp listener; there is no HTTP endpoint.
arms.install_hint: Unity Package Manager git URL https://github.com/CoderGamester/mcp-unity.git (the package builds the Node bridge itself)

steps.text: Confirm Node 18+ is present.
Add the UPM package.

Open the project and let the import finish. On load the package runs npm install + npm run build in <package>/Server~. If Server~/build/index.js is missing, use Tools > MCP Unity > Server Window > 'Force Install Server'.
Tools > MCP Unity > Server Window > 'Configure <client>' — it writes the absolute path and MCP_UNITY_SETTINGS_PATH for you.
Tools > MCP Unity > Server Window > 'Start Server' (AutoStartServer defaults to true).

install.repair_command: cd <package>/Server~ && npm install && npm run build
install.note: There is no one-line install: the Node bridge is not published for npx and is built by the Unity package at Editor load. Do NOT run `npx mcp-unity-server` -- that npm package is a stale 1.0.0 from April 2025 by the same author, four minor versions behind the 1.4.0 package, and it resolves, so it looks plausible and runs the wrong code. The trailing tilde in `Server~` is required (Unity ignores `~` folders). The package-cache path carries a version hash that changes on every update and silently breaks a hard-coded client config -- re-run the Configure button after updating. Port 8090 is overridable with UNITY_PORT; UNITY_HOST defaults to localhost. README says Unity 6+, package.json enforces 2022.3. Entering Play Mode triggers a domain reload that drops the bridge.
